jobs.title: Vice President, Operations
jobs.description:
Description

Poste chez Vision Group

VICE PRESIDENT, OPERATIONS

Lead performance. Develop leaders. Shape the future of clinic operations.

Working at Vision Group’s head office means joining one of North America’s leading vision correction providers. You will contribute to the growth of an organization supporting more than 11 brands and 60 clinics across Canada and the United States.

Join our team, where our Great Place to Work® certification reflects our commitment to creating a supportive and inclusive workplace.

Your Mandate

The Vice President of Operations leads the operational performance and ongoing development of Vision Group’s national clinic network. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this executive translates business strategy into consistent clinic execution, strengthens operational leadership, and builds a scalable operating model that supports exceptional patient care and sustainable growth.

The mandate centres on four priorities: performance, people, patient flow, and execution. Working closely with clinical and corporate partners, the Vice President aligns resources, operating standards, and management practices to drive consistent performance while responding to regional needs and clinical realities.

The position requires regular travel across the clinic network.

Your tasks at a glance

Operational Strategy and Performance

Develop and execute the clinic operations strategy in alignment with organizational priorities.
Establish operational goals, budgets, performance indicators, and accountability across regional, district, and clinic leadership.
Oversee productivity, capacity utilization, labour efficiency, conversion, patient experience, and operating costs.
Translate financial and operational data into actionable insights, corrective plans, and measurable improvements.
Establish consistent performance reviews and follow-up practices across the network.

Leadership and Organizational Development

Lead, coach, and develop Regional and District Operations leaders, strengthening their ability to deliver results through clinic teams.
Establish clear expectations, effective delegation, and consistent performance management across the operations organization.
Partner with Talent & Culture on workforce planning, leadership development, succession planning, and employee engagement.
Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement, ensuring leaders have the tools and support to succeed.

Patient Flow and Capacity Optimization

Align clinic staffing, scheduling, and capacity with patient demand and business priorities.
Improve the patient journey from consultation and pre-operative assessment through surgery and post-operative follow-up.
Address bottlenecks affecting patient access, experience, throughput, and conversion in partnership with Medical Affairs and clinical leaders, while respecting clinical judgment and patient safety.

Operating Model and Continuous Improvement

Develop scalable operating standards, processes, and management practices, balancing network-wide consistency with local requirements.
Identify effective practices, support their adoption across clinics, and measure their sustained impact.
Partner with Technology and Business Intelligence to improve reporting, decision-making, and operational workflows.

Transformation, Integration, and Growth

Lead the operational delivery of transformation initiatives, clinic integrations, expansions, and new programs.
Establish implementation plans, ownership, timelines, resource requirements, and success measures while managing operational readiness, risks, and dependencies.
Work with Medical Affairs, Finance, Talent & Culture, Marketing, Technology, Business Intelligence, Procurement, and Risk Management to ensure initiatives are adopted at clinic level and deliver measurable benefits.

A clear view of your assets

You bring progressive senior leadership experience overseeing a complex, geographically dispersed, multi-site organization.
You have successfully led regional or district leaders and delivered measurable operational improvements through local management teams.
You have experience in healthcare, ambulatory care, or another service environment with significant staffing, scheduling, and capacity requirements.
You demonstrate strong financial and analytical capabilities, including operational budgeting, forecasting, labour planning, and performance management.
You have built scalable operating practices and led organizational change through implementation and sustained adoption.
You have experience supporting acquisitions, integrations, or network expansion.
You hold a bachelor’s degree in business administration, healthcare management, operations, or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Your leadership approach

You build leaders: You develop capable teams, delegate effectively, and strengthen decision-making throughout the organization.
You drive performance: You understand operational and financial drivers, address performance gaps, and follow through on commitments.
You think systemically: You connect people, processes, capacity, technology, and patient needs when making decisions.
You lead change: You establish ownership, build commitment, and sustain new ways of working.
You influence effectively: You communicate clearly and build productive relationships with clinic teams, clinical partners, and executive leadership.
You exercise sound judgment: You balance patient care, employee experience, operational needs, and business performance.

From our point of view

This is an opportunity to shape how Vision Group’s clinic network operates and grows. You will develop leaders, strengthen execution, and build the operating model that supports our next stage of growth while keeping exceptional patient care at its centre.

If you bring the operational discipline, leadership, and vision to guide this next chapter, we invite you to apply.

jobs.title: SOX Director - ITGC
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a SOX Director – ITGC based in Canada .

The SOX Director – ITGC will lead the strategy, design, and oversight of the enterprise IT SOX compliance program, serving as the senior technical authority for IT controls. This is a hands-on leadership role covering IT General Controls (ITGCs), IT Application Controls (ITACs), and controls related to private key management and digital asset custody. Operating in a complex, rapidly evolving financial technology environment, the successful candidate will build scalable control frameworks that support modern cloud infrastructure, continuous deployment, and blockchain-native systems without unnecessarily slowing engineering teams. The role requires close collaboration with Finance, Engineering, Security, Infrastructure, Internal Audit, and external auditors. It also carries significant executive visibility, including responsibility for communicating control risks, remediation progress, and the organization's overall IT control posture to senior leadership and the Audit Committee.

Accountabilities

Own the enterprise IT SOX strategy and roadmap, covering ITGCs, ITACs, and digital asset and private key management controls across relevant entities and jurisdictions.
Develop and maintain the IT SOX control framework, including scoping methodologies, risk assessments, control design standards, testing approaches, and evidence requirements.
Determine the applications, infrastructure, wallet and custody systems, third-party providers, and service-organization dependencies that fall within the SOX program's scope.
Design practical, effective controls that align with modern engineering environments, including cloud infrastructure, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD), and infrastructure as code.
Establish standards for management testing and evidence quality, oversee co-sourced and matrixed resources, and review the quality and consistency of their work.
Introduce AI-enabled workflows, continuous controls monitoring, and data analytics to improve assurance efficiency and move beyond periodic manual testing.
Own SOX control design and coverage across the complete private key lifecycle, including key generation, storage, access, signing and approval workflows, rotation, backup, recovery, and retirement.
Assess controls over digital asset custody architectures, including hardware security modules (HSMs), multi-party computation (MPC), multi-signature arrangements, and hot, warm, and cold wallet structures.
Evaluate segregation of duties, quorum and approval requirements, privileged access, and other safeguards within key management and custody environments.
Assess how private key and custody controls support the existence, completeness, and safeguarding of customer and corporate digital assets, including their financial reporting implications.
Evaluate controls over on-chain and off-chain transaction processing, wallet-to-ledger reconciliations, blockchain data dependencies, and relationships with third-party custodians and service organizations.
Monitor emerging digital asset risks and adapt the SOX control framework as products, blockchain networks, and custody models evolve.
Lead the assessment of control deficiencies, including root cause analysis, severity and pervasiveness assessments, and recommendations for classification as control deficiencies, significant deficiencies, or material weaknesses.
Own remediation strategies for outstanding ITGC and key management findings, driving accountability and timely resolution with Engineering, Security, and Infrastructure leaders.
Escalate significant control gaps and remediation delays to senior leadership and report progress to the Audit Committee when required.
Coordinate with Internal Audit to ensure remediated controls are appropriately documented and ready for independent validation.
Serve as the senior SOX advisor to the CFO, CISO, CTO, Controller, and Audit Committee on IT control posture, emerging risks, and remediation priorities.
Lead external auditor engagement on IT matters, including audit strategy, scoping and reliance decisions, walkthroughs, and resolution of disagreements.
Advise Engineering and Security leaders by translating audit and compliance requirements into practical technical and operational control decisions.
Collaborate with Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), business process SOX leaders, and co-sourced providers to coordinate coverage across the broader assurance program.
Mentor SOX and risk professionals, strengthening technical expertise and raising the overall quality of the function.

Requirements

Professional experience: 10+ years of experience in SOX compliance, IT audit, internal audit, or external audit, with deep ITGC expertise and a demonstrated record of leading enterprise-scale programs.
Mandatory crypto expertise: Direct, hands-on experience designing, assessing, or auditing controls related to cryptocurrency private key management, wallet infrastructure, signing workflows, digital asset custody, and asset safeguarding. This is an essential requirement.
Industry background: Experience in a cryptocurrency exchange, digital asset custodian, fintech, payments company, or similarly complex and rapidly evolving technology environment.
Certifications: CISA and CPA certifications are required. Candidates holding one certification and actively pursuing the other may also be considered.
SOX and audit frameworks: Expert knowledge of ITGC frameworks, SOX Section 404, COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB standards, with the ability to make and defend decisions involving control scope, audit reliance, and deficiency classification.
Technical understanding: Strong knowledge of systems architecture, databases, cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and the technical environments supporting enterprise applications.
Financial reporting awareness: Ability to connect ITGC or private key management control failures to business process controls, financial reporting risks, and potential financial statement impacts.
Auditor and executive engagement: Experience managing relationships with external auditors, with Big Four experience preferred, and presenting control matters to Audit Committees and senior executives.
International experience: Experience working across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions, or complex organizational structures.
Leadership and communication: Strong stakeholder management, mentoring, and influencing skills, with the ability to establish credibility with both technical engineering teams and senior Finance leaders.
Preferred program experience: Experience establishing or scaling an IT SOX program in a growth-stage organization or a company entering its first year of SOX compliance.
Preferred technical knowledge: Familiarity with CI/CD processes, GitLab or comparable version-control platforms, and cloud environments such as AWS and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
Third-party assurance: Familiarity with SOC 1 and SOC 2 reliance arrangements, third-party custodians, service providers, and proof-of-reserves or similar attestations.
Compliance technology: Experience with audit and governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms such as AuditBoard or Workiva is an asset.
Emerging technologies: Familiarity with AI-assisted compliance tools and an interest in adopting new technologies to improve audit and assurance processes.

Benefits

Remote work: Full-time remote position, with Canada included among the eligible locations.
Annual target salary: USD $116,600–$259,700. The advertised range is a target annual salary range and may vary according to skills, experience, and the scope of the role.
Additional compensation: Eligibility for additional compensation through bonus and equity programs.
Wellness allowance: Additional wellness support is included in the compensation package.
Healthcare and retirement benefits: Medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) benefits are listed for eligible U.S. employees only; these should not be assumed to apply to Canadian employees.
Compensation flexibility: Final compensation is determined based on relevant experience, skills, and role responsibilities.
Global collaboration: Opportunity to work with international teams across Finance, Engineering, Security, and digital asset infrastructure.
Professional impact: Senior-level ownership of a complex SOX program, with direct exposure to executive leadership, external auditors, and emerging digital asset control challenges.

How Jobgether Works

We use an AI-powered matching process
to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

We appreciate your interest and wish you the best!

Why Apply Through Jobgether?

Data Privacy Notice:
By submitting your application, you acknowledge that Jobgether will process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy and share relevant information with the hiring employer. This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). You may exercise your rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection) at any time.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
